Chief_Complaint.content: Patient reports feeling unwell for about five days with a cough and cold symptoms.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: I haven't been feeling well, for, a good few days, now... I just feel a bit, run-down, you know I've got, a cough, a cold.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Symptoms started about five days ago (on Saturday).
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: it would have been that, Saturday. So, what's that about five, five days ago? Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has a mostly dry cough, which can be productive of a small amount of phlegm in the morning.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: mostly, dry it's a , you know it's a wee bit in the morning it's a bit worse... So you're not bringing up any mucky, flem? Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports a runny nose (sniffles) and a sore throat.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Yeah, I can certainly hear you've got the sniffles. So, bit of a runny, bit of a runny nose... I've, I've had a bit of a sore throat.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is experiencing shortness of breath.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: your, your breathing is fine is it? No it's, it's, it's, it's not, it's not good... So you're , you're, you're feeling more short of breath? Yeah, yeah.
any pain in your chest at all? No, no

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports feeling hot and cold and having sweats, but has not measured a temperature.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Yeah, yeah that's, that's, that's, that's definitely something I've noticed. Like, you know in, in bed with the wife and having to, you know get out and... I haven't, haven't, you know, used a thermometer or anything.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient experienced diarrhea on the first day of illness, which has since resolved.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: the first, the first day I had... a wee bit of diarrhoea... but that, that's fine, now.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports generalized stiffness and aching in joints like elbows and knees.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I have, I have noticed like when I, you know, when I'm bending down and... just a wee bit stiffer than, than normal... It it's, just kinda, like you know when you're, when you're bending like, elbows and knees

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has some hearing dullness but attributes it to age.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Uh, yeah, , a, a wee bit I mean... my hearing's, you know it's not as good as it used to be

Past_Medical_History.source_text: I've got the uh, I've got the diabetes... Uh, it's, it's uh, type, two, two.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has been diagnosed with high blood pressure (hypertension).
Past_Medical_History.source_text: he, took my blood pressure and that said that was, that was high, uh, high, higher than it should be.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient describes himself as overweight ('on the chunky side').
Past_Medical_History.source_text: I'm a wee bit, on the chunky side.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Patient reports no known allergies to medications.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: No, nothing, nothing that, nothing that I'm aware of

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is 50 years old and lives with his wife; his children have moved out.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I'm fifty years old now... now it's just me and the missus... kids, the kids have uh, they've flown the nest.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works in a factory manufacturing steel parts.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: there's a wee factory... we just manufacture like uh... kind of steel, steel parts

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient smokes occasionally and is trying to cut down using a vaporizer.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: a wee, every now and again, but I'm, I, I am trying to cut that down. I've got a wee uh... The wee vaporisers.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks approximately 9 pints of beer per week (more than 14 units/week).
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: maybe what like four, four pints on like Saturday and then, you know on, Sunday as well... Nine, nine pints in a week, I would say.

Assessment.content: The impression is a viral illness, possibly an upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) or early influenza, with a potential for a secondary lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI).
Assessment.source_text: I think you know what you essentially have is a bit of a, a bit of a viral illness perhaps, a bit of a, maybe early signs of a flu... I don't think you've got a chest infection, but what we could think about is...

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised conservative management including rest, drinking plenty of fluids, and taking regular Paracetamol for fever/sweats.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: stay rested, drink plenty of fluids... taking regular Paracetamol would be beneficial.

Plan_of_Care.content: A delayed prescription for Amoxicillin (one tablet three times a day) was provided, to be started in 24-48 hours only if symptoms do not improve.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I'll give you a script today, give it about twenty four to forty eight hours. If you feel like you're still feeling breathless and, run-down, I think there's no harm in starting a course of antibiotics, something like Amoxicillin. One tablet, three times a day.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review next week if still not better.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: and , if you're still not better by next week, come back and see me, we can have another look.
